revealWordProblem.title: Apply: Budgets
revealWordProblem.text:
The parking lot shown is being repaved. Asphalt for the parking lot costs $3.95 per square foot, and labor costs about $3 per square foot.
Question: What total budget do you recommend for repaving the parking lot? Show how you found the area.
revealWordProblem.imageAlt: A diagram of a parking lot made of a rectangle and a trapezoid, labeled 25 feet, 70 feet, 57 feet, 40 feet, and 54 feet.
revealWordProblem.sampleAnswer: Decompose the lot into a rectangle and a trapezoid, find each area from the labeled lengths, and add them for the total area in square feet. Paving and labor together cost $3.95 + $3.00 = $6.95 for every square foot, so multiply the total area by $6.95. I would recommend rounding that total up so the budget still covers the job if the crew needs a little extra material.

conceptIntro.heading: Push further — How do we find the area of a trapezoid?
conceptIntro.intro: You already can do this. So we go up a level, not up a number: find what is always true, show it a second way, and be ready to defend it with a reason instead of an answer.
conceptIntro.keyIdea: Area of a trapezoid = ½ × (base 1 + base 2) × height. We add the two bases first, then take half — and you can say why it is true, and where it would stop being true.

iDo.title: Watch me
lines: My trapezoid window has a top base of 4 feet, a bottom base of 8 feet, and a height of 5 feet.
I write the formula: A = ½ × (b1 + b2) × h.
I take half: ½ × 60 = 30. So the area is 30 square feet.
linesEs: Mi ventana trapezoidal tiene una base superior de 4 pies, una base inferior de 8 pies y una altura de 5 pies.
Escribo la fórmula: A = ½ × (b1 + b2) × h.
Tomo la mitad: ½ × 60 = 30. Entonces el área es 30 pies cuadrados.

weDo.title: Try it together — then prove it
lines: Now a smaller trapezoid: bases 3 cm and 5 cm, height 2 cm.
Now take half: ½ × 16 = 8, so the area is 8 square centimeters.
Now prove it: say why that move had to work at all — not just that it did.
Sentence frame — convince a skeptic: "My method works because ___ . It would stop working if ___ ."
linesEs: Ahora un trapecio más pequeño: bases de 3 cm y 5 cm, altura de 2 cm.
Ahora toma la mitad: ½ × 16 = 8, así que el área es 8 centímetros cuadrados.
Ahora demuéstralo: di por qué ese paso tenía que funcionar — no solo que funcionó.
Marco de oración — convence a alguien que duda: «Mi método funciona porque ___ . Dejaría de funcionar si ___ .»

youDo.title: Now you try — and defend it
lines: Try the problems below on your own. Getting the answer is half the work — be ready to say why your method works, and where it would stop working.
Then pick one problem and show it a second way. If two different methods agree, that agreement is your proof.
linesEs: Intenta los problemas de abajo por tu cuenta. Obtener la respuesta es la mitad del trabajo — prepárate para decir por qué funciona tu método y dónde dejaría de funcionar.
Luego elige un problema y muéstralo de una segunda manera. Si dos métodos distintos coinciden, esa coincidencia es tu prueba.

conceptIntro.headingEs: Ve más allá — ¿Cómo hallamos el área de un trapecio?
conceptIntro.introEs: Esto ya lo sabes hacer. Así que subimos de nivel, no de número: halla lo que siempre es cierto, muéstralo de una segunda manera y prepárate para defenderlo con una razón en lugar de una respuesta.
conceptIntro.keyIdeaEs: Área de un trapecio = ½ × (base 1 + base 2) × altura. Primero sumamos las dos bases y luego tomamos la mitad — y puedes decir por qué es cierto y dónde dejaría de serlo.

onLevel.title: Using the Wrong Height

workedExample.label: Read the blueprint
workedExample.work: A trapezoid window has b1 = 7 ft and b2 = 13 ft. The slanted side measures 10 ft, and the straight-up height between the bases is 6 ft.
workedExample.workEs: Una ventana trapezoidal tiene b1 = 7 pies y b2 = 13 pies. El lado inclinado mide 10 pies, y la altura recta entre las bases es 6 pies.

onLevel.correctWork: The student used the slanted side (10 ft) as the height instead of the true perpendicular height (6 ft). The height in the trapezoid formula must be measured straight up between the two bases, not along the slanted side. The correct area is A = ½ × (7 + 13) × 6 = ½ × 20 × 6 = 60 sq ft, not 100 sq ft.
hints: Look at which measurement was used for h. Is it the straight-up distance between the bases, or the slanted edge?
The height must form a right angle with both bases. A slanted side is longer than the true height and will make the area too big.
onLevel.explanation: The 10 ft slanted side was substituted for the height, but the height of a trapezoid is the straight-up perpendicular distance between the two bases, which is 6 ft here. Using the true height gives A = ½ × (7 + 13) × 6 = ½ × 20 × 6 = 60 sq ft; the slant is always longer, which is why 100 sq ft came out too big.
onLevel.explanationEs: Se sustituyó el lado inclinado de 10 ft por la altura, pero la altura de un trapecio es la distancia perpendicular, hacia arriba, entre las dos bases, que aquí mide 6 ft. Con la altura verdadera: A = ½ × (7 + 13) × 6 = ½ × 20 × 6 = 60 pies cuadrados; el lado inclinado siempre es más largo, por eso 100 pies cuadrados salió demasiado grande.
onLevel.correctWorkEs: El estudiante usó el lado inclinado (10 pies) como la altura en lugar de la verdadera altura perpendicular (6 pies). La altura en la fórmula del trapecio se mide recta entre las dos bases, no a lo largo del lado inclinado. El área correcta es A = ½ × (7 + 13) × 6 = ½ × 20 × 6 = 60 pies cuadrados, no 100 pies cuadrados.
hintsEs: Mira qué medida se usó para h. ¿Es la distancia recta entre las bases, o la arista inclinada?
La altura debe formar un ángulo recto con las dos bases. Un lado inclinado es más largo que la altura verdadera y hará que el área salga demasiado grande.

onLevel.title: Find the Area Error

workedExample.label: Identify the bases and height
workedExample.work: b₁ = 10 m, b₂ = 6 m, h = 7 m
workedExample.labelEs: Identifica las bases y la altura
workedExample.workEs: b₁ = 10 m, b₂ = 6 m, h = 7 m

onLevel.correctWork: The student forgot to multiply by ½. A = ½ × 16 × 7 = ½ × 112 = 56 sq m.
hints: Look at Step 4. What happened to the ½?
The student skipped the ½ and just multiplied (b₁ + b₂) × h.
onLevel.explanation: The ½ appears in the formula and in the substitution, then disappears in the final calculation. Keeping it gives A = ½ × 16 × 7 = ½ × 112 = 56 sq m, which is exactly half of the 112 that was reported.
onLevel.explanationEs: El ½ aparece en la fórmula y en la sustitución, y luego desaparece en el cálculo final. Al conservarlo: A = ½ × 16 × 7 = ½ × 112 = 56 metros cuadrados, que es exactamente la mitad de los 112 que se reportaron.
onLevel.correctWorkEs: El estudiante olvidó multiplicar por ½. A = ½ × 16 × 7 = ½ × 112 = 56 m cuadrados.
hintsEs: Mira el Paso 4. ¿Qué pasó con el ½?
El estudiante se saltó el ½ y solo multiplicó (b₁ + b₂) × h.

onLevel.prompt: A trapezoid and a parallelogram both have a height of 8 ft. The trapezoid has bases of 5 ft and 11 ft. The parallelogram has a base of 7 ft. Which shape has the greater area? Explain your reasoning using the formulas.
onLevel.sentenceFrame: The trapezoid's area is ___ because ½ × (___ + ___) × ___ = ___. The parallelogram's area is ___ because ___ × ___ = ___. The ___ has a greater area by ___ sq ft.
onLevel.hint: Write out A = (b1 + b2) ÷ 2 × h with the bases you know; solve for h when the area changes.
hints: Both shapes share a height of 8 ft, so the real contest is between the base measurements.
Find each area with its own formula: trapezoid ½ × (5 + 11) × 8, parallelogram 7 × 8. Then compare the results.
Compute ½ × 16 × 8 for the trapezoid and 7 × 8 for the parallelogram, then subtract to say how much greater one is.
onLevel.explanation: The trapezoid's area is ½ × (5 + 11) × 8 = ½ × 16 × 8 = 64 sq ft and the parallelogram's is 7 × 8 = 56 sq ft, so the trapezoid is greater by 8 sq ft. Since both shapes share the height of 8 ft, the comparison really comes down to the trapezoid's average base, ½ × (5 + 11) = 8 ft, against the parallelogram's base of 7 ft.
onLevel.explanationEs: El área del trapecio es ½ × (5 + 11) × 8 = ½ × 16 × 8 = 64 pies cuadrados y la del paralelogramo es 7 × 8 = 56 pies cuadrados, así que el trapecio es mayor por 8 pies cuadrados. Como las dos figuras comparten la altura de 8 ft, la comparación se reduce a la base promedio del trapecio, ½ × (5 + 11) = 8 ft, frente a la base de 7 ft del paralelogramo.
onLevel.promptEs: Un trapecio y un paralelogramo tienen los dos una altura de 8 pies. El trapecio tiene bases de 5 pies y 11 pies. El paralelogramo tiene una base de 7 pies. ¿Cuál figura tiene mayor área? Explica tu razonamiento usando las fórmulas.
hintsEs: Ambas figuras comparten una altura de 8 pies, así que la verdadera competencia está entre las medidas de las bases.
Halla cada área con su propia fórmula: trapecio ½ × (5 + 11) × 8, paralelogramo 7 × 8. Luego compara los resultados.
Calcula ½ × 16 × 8 para el trapecio y 7 × 8 para el paralelogramo, y luego resta para decir cuánto mayor es uno.

onLevel.stem: Blueprint 1: A trapezoidal lobby window has bases of 6 ft and 10 ft and a height of 4 ft. What is its area for the glass order?
onLevel.explanation: Start with the formula: A = ½ × (b1 + b2) × h. Put in the numbers: ½ × (6 + 10) × 4. Add the bases first: ½ × 16 × 4. Multiply: 32 sq ft.
choiceFeedback: 16 just adds the bases 6 + 10. The height and the divide-by-2 have not happened yet.
40 is 10 × 4 — only the longer base times the height. The 6-ft base has to join in before anything is halved.
60 multiplies the two bases together. The formula never multiplies base × base — pair the AVERAGE of the bases with the height.
onLevel.stemEs: Plano 1: una ventana trapezoidal del vestíbulo tiene bases de 6 ft y 10 ft y una altura de 4 ft. ¿Cuál es su área para el pedido de vidrio?
onLevel.explanationEs: Empieza con la fórmula: A = ½ × (b1 + b2) × h. Sustituye los números: ½ × (6 + 10) × 4. Suma primero las bases: ½ × 16 × 4. Multiplica: 32 ft cuadrados.
hints: A trapezoid's bases are its two parallel sides, and the height is the perpendicular distance between them.
Use A = ½ × (b1 + b2) × h: add the bases, multiply by the height, then take half.
Add 6 + 10 = 16, multiply that sum by the height of 4, and then find half of the product.
hintsEs: Las bases de un trapecio son sus dos lados paralelos, y la altura es la distancia perpendicular entre ellos.
Usa A = ½ × (b1 + b2) × h: suma las bases, multiplica por la altura y luego toma la mitad.
Suma 6 + 10 = 16, multiplica esa suma por la altura de 4 y después halla la mitad del producto.

extending.hint: Use A = (b1 + b2) ÷ 2 × h for each trapezoid; when the area is given, work backwards to the missing measurement.
hints: Windows A and B are missing area, but Windows C and D are missing a base — those need backwards work.
Missing area: ½ × (b₁ + b₂) × h. Missing base: double the area, divide by the height, then subtract the base you know.
Window C: 2 × 72 = 144, then 144 ÷ 8 = 18 is the base sum — subtract the 10 ft base to get Base 2.
extending.explanation: Windows A and B use the formula forward: ½ × (8 + 4) × 5 = 30 sq ft and ½ × (12 + 6) × 4 = 36 sq ft. Windows C and D run it backwards — double the area, divide by the height, then subtract the base you know: 144 ÷ 8 = 18 and 18 − 10 = 8 ft for Window C; 96 ÷ 6 = 16 and 16 − 5 = 11 ft for Window D.
extending.explanationEs: Las Ventanas A y B usan la fórmula hacia adelante: ½ × (8 + 4) × 5 = 30 pies cuadrados y ½ × (12 + 6) × 4 = 36 pies cuadrados. Las Ventanas C y D la usan al revés: duplica el área, divide entre la altura y resta la base que ya conoces: 144 ÷ 8 = 18 y 18 − 10 = 8 ft para la Ventana C; 96 ÷ 6 = 16 y 16 − 5 = 11 ft para la Ventana D.
hintsEs: A las Ventanas A y B les falta el área, pero a las Ventanas C y D les falta una base: esas necesitan trabajo al revés.
Falta el área: ½ × (b₁ + b₂) × h. Falta una base: duplica el área, divide entre la altura y luego resta la base que conoces.
Ventana C: 2 × 72 = 144, luego 144 ÷ 8 = 18 es la suma de las bases; resta la base de 10 pies para obtener la Base 2.

extending.label: Match each shape to its area.
extending.hint: Compute area for each shape, then compare to sort them.
hints: Three different rules appear here: trapezoids, a triangle, a parallelogram, and a rectangle each have their own formula.
Trapezoid: ½ × (b₁ + b₂) × h. Triangle: ½ × b × h. Parallelogram and rectangle: just multiply.
Start with the first trapezoid: ½ × (10 + 6) × 4. Work each shape's area, then match it to its card.
extending.explanation: Each shape needs its own rule. The three trapezoids give ½ × (10 + 6) × 4 = 32, ½ × (8 + 4) × 5 = 30, and ½ × (12 + 8) × 4 = 40 sq units. The triangle is ½ × 14 × 6 = 42, the parallelogram is 9 × 5 = 45, and the rectangle is 7 × 3 = 21 sq units.
extending.explanationEs: Cada figura necesita su propia regla. Los tres trapecios dan ½ × (10 + 6) × 4 = 32, ½ × (8 + 4) × 5 = 30 y ½ × (12 + 8) × 4 = 40 unidades cuadradas. El triángulo es ½ × 14 × 6 = 42, el paralelogramo es 9 × 5 = 45 y el rectángulo es 7 × 3 = 21 unidades cuadradas.
extending.labelEs: Une cada figura con su área.
hintsEs: Aquí aparecen tres reglas distintas: los trapecios, un triángulo, un paralelogramo y un rectángulo tienen cada uno su fórmula.
Trapecio: ½ × (b₁ + b₂) × h. Triángulo: ½ × b × h. Paralelogramo y rectángulo: solo multiplica.
Empieza con el primer trapecio: ½ × (10 + 6) × 4. Calcula el área de cada figura y luego únela con su tarjeta.

extending.stem: Blueprint 2: A trapezoidal skylight has bases of 9 ft and 7 ft and a height of 6 ft. What is its area?
choiceFeedback: Is the perpendicular height 6?
You computed base × height; now divide by 2.
A triangle is half a rectangle.
extending.stemEs: Plano 2: un tragaluz trapezoidal tiene bases de 9 ft y 7 ft y una altura de 6 ft. ¿Cuál es su área?
hints: The order of the bases does not matter — adding them gives the same sum either way.
Follow A = ½ × (b1 + b2) × h in order: add, multiply by the height, then halve.
9 + 7 = 16. Multiply 16 by the height of 6, then take half of that result.
hintsEs: El orden de las bases no importa: sumarlas da el mismo resultado en cualquier orden.
Sigue A = ½ × (b1 + b2) × h en orden: suma, multiplica por la altura y luego toma la mitad.
9 + 7 = 16. Multiplica 16 por la altura de 6 y después toma la mitad de ese resultado.

extending.stem: Two equal trapezoid windows join to form a parallelogram with area 96 sq ft. What is the area of ONE trapezoid?
extending.explanation: One trapezoid is half the parallelogram: 96 ÷ 2 = 48 sq ft. This matches A = ½ × (5 + 11) × 6 = ½ × 16 × 6 = 48 sq ft — the ½ comes from the trapezoid being half of the parallelogram.
choiceFeedback: 16 ft is the combined base, not the trapezoid's area.
That's the whole parallelogram — ONE trapezoid is half of it.
You doubled instead of halving — one trapezoid is half of 96.
extending.stemEs: Dos ventanas trapezoidales iguales se unen para formar un paralelogramo con un área de 96 ft cuadrados. ¿Cuál es el área de UN trapecio?
extending.explanationEs: Un trapecio es la mitad del paralelogramo: 96 ÷ 2 = 48 ft cuadrados. Esto coincide con A = ½ × (5 + 11) × 6 = ½ × 16 × 6 = 48 ft cuadrados; el ½ viene de que el trapecio es la mitad del paralelogramo.
hints: Two identical trapezoids fit together to make one parallelogram — that is where the ½ in the formula comes from.

extending.stem: A trapezoid has an area of 45 sq ft, bases of 7 ft and 11 ft. What is the height?
extending.explanation: Start with the formula: A = ½ × (b₁ + b₂) × h. Put in what you know: 45 = ½ × 18 × h. Simplify the right side: 45 = 9h. Divide both sides by 9: h = 5 ft.
choiceFeedback: Check it: (7 + 11) ÷ 2 × 3 = 27, not 45. Double the area first: 2 × 45 = 90, then ÷ 18.
Check it: (7 + 11) ÷ 2 × 10 = 90 — that's double the area. Divide 90 by 18, not by 9.
hints: You already know the area (45 sq ft) and both bases (7 ft and 11 ft) — the height is what's missing.
Simplify first: ½ × (7 + 11) = 9. So the equation becomes 45 = 9 × h.
Divide 45 by 9 to find the height in feet.
extending.stemEs: Un trapecio tiene un área de 45 ft cuadrados y bases de 7 ft y 11 ft. ¿Cuál es la altura?
extending.explanationEs: Empieza con la fórmula: A = ½ × (b₁ + b₂) × h. Sustituye lo que sabes: 45 = ½ × 18 × h. Simplifica el lado derecho: 45 = 9h. Divide ambos lados entre 9: h = 5 ft.
hintsEs: Ya conoces el área (45 pies²) y ambas bases (7 pies y 11 pies): lo que falta es la altura.
Simplifica primero: ½ × (7 + 11) = 9. Así la ecuación se vuelve 45 = 9 × h.
Divide 45 entre 9 para hallar la altura en pies.

extending.stem: Design a trapezoid whose area is exactly 24 sq ft, where one base is 4 ft LONGER than the other. Give both bases and the height, and show your design checks out. Could a classmate's correct design use different numbers than yours?
extending.stemEs: Diseña un trapecio cuya área sea exactamente 24 pies², donde una base sea 4 pies MÁS LARGA que la otra. Da las dos bases y la altura, y demuestra que tu diseño cumple. ¿Podría el diseño correcto de un compañero usar números distintos a los tuyos?
extending.modelAnswer: Bases 4 ft and 8 ft with height 4 ft: (4 + 8) ÷ 2 = 6, and 6 × 4 = 24 sq ft ✓. Yes — a classmate could use bases 2 ft and 6 ft with height 6 ft: (2 + 6) ÷ 2 = 4, and 4 × 6 = 24 sq ft. Any base pair 4 apart whose average divides 24 gives a valid height.
extending.modelAnswerEs: Bases de 4 y 8 pies con altura 4: (4 + 8) ÷ 2 = 6, y 6 × 4 = 24 pies² ✓. Sí — un compañero podría usar bases de 2 y 6 con altura 6: (2 + 6) ÷ 2 = 4, y 4 × 6 = 24 pies². Cualquier par de bases con diferencia 4 cuya media divida a 24 da una altura válida.

practice.commonMistake: A common mistake in Area of Trapezoids is forgetting the ½ in A = ½ × (b1 + b2) × h. After adding the bases and multiplying by the height, students stop there instead of taking half — for example, with bases 6 ft and 10 ft and a height of 4 ft, they compute (6 + 10) × 4 = 64 sq ft instead of taking half to get the correct 32 sq ft. That unhalved number is really the area of the parallelogram made from two trapezoids, not the area of one trapezoid. Before you submit, always ask: "Did I take half of my last answer?"

connect.scenario: A builder is pouring concrete for a trapezoidal driveway. The driveway has parallel edges of 20 feet and 12 feet with a height of 15 feet. One bag of concrete covers 6 square feet.
connect.promptQuestion: How many bags of concrete does the builder need?
connect.prompt: The driveway's area is ___ sq ft because A = 1/2 x (___ + ___) x ___. He needs ___ bags because ___ / 6 = ___.

check.stem: What is the area of the trapezoidal driveway?
check.explanation: Start with the formula: A = ½ × (b₁ + b₂) × h. Put in the numbers: ½ × (20 + 12) × 15. Add the bases first: ½ × 32 × 15. Multiply: 240 sq ft.
check.stemEs: ¿Cuál es el área de la entrada en forma de trapecio?
check.explanationEs: Empieza con la fórmula: A = ½ × (b₁ + b₂) × h. Pon los números: ½ × (20 + 12) × 15. Suma las bases primero: ½ × 32 × 15. Multiplica: 240 pies cuadrados.

check.stem: How many bags of concrete does the builder need?
check.explanation: Each bag covers 6 sq ft, so 240 ÷ 6 = 40 bags.
check.stemEs: ¿Cuántas bolsas de concreto necesita el constructor?
check.explanationEs: Cada bolsa cubre 6 pies cuadrados, así que 240 ÷ 6 = 40 bolsas.

check.stem: Why add the two parallel edges and then take half?
choices: Because trapezoids are half of rectangles
Because the average of the two bases acts like one rectangle's width
Because the height must be halved
check.explanation: (20 + 12) ÷ 2 = 16 is the average base. Multiplying that average by the height 15 gives 240 — the same as ½ × (b₁ + b₂) × h.
check.stemEs: ¿Por qué sumar los dos bordes paralelos y luego tomar la mitad?
check.explanationEs: (20 + 12) ÷ 2 = 16 es la base promedio. Multiplicar ese promedio por la altura 15 da 240 — lo mismo que ½ × (b₁ + b₂) × h.
choicesEs: Porque los trapecios son la mitad de los rectángulos
Porque el promedio de las dos bases funciona como el ancho de un rectángulo
Porque la altura se debe dividir a la mitad

connect.modelAnswer: A = ½ × (20 + 12) × 15 = ½ × 32 × 15 = 240 sq ft. At 6 sq ft per bag, the builder needs 240 ÷ 6 = 40 bags.

connect.scenarioEs: Un constructor está vaciando concreto para una entrada de auto en forma de trapecio. La entrada tiene bordes paralelos de 20 pies y 12 pies con una altura de 15 pies. Una bolsa de concreto cubre 6 pies cuadrados.
connect.promptQuestionEs: ¿Cuántas bolsas de concreto necesita el constructor?
connect.modelAnswerEs: A = ½ × (20 + 12) × 15 = ½ × 32 × 15 = 240 pies cuadrados. A 6 pies cuadrados por bolsa, el constructor necesita 240 ÷ 6 = 40 bolsas.

The height is always half the base
A triangle is half of a parallelogram with the same base and height

choiceFeedback: This confuses the ½ in the formula with counting sides — it isn't about how many sides a triangle has.
